Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect both required wake views and the fish-control shelf before proposing any policy change. I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to ground the edit in the rollout visuals and `fish-control-primitives` because this is the required structured transfer point.

The evidence confirms all four rollouts use direct, quiescent initialization. I’m comparing the long-lived `5.156L` approach against the naive and target-aware upper-curl failures; next I’m checking both rows of their combined sheets and tying the visible turn topology back to trajectory and actuator signals.

Both visual rows agree on the key distinction: the parent’s anterior half-cycle mechanism creates a stable long translating wake, while the naive and newer bearing/course variants fold into the same tight upward exit. The shelf consultation now matters because the inherited evidence has exhausted static curvature, posterior asymmetry, instantaneous yaw closure, direct bearing dominance, and velocity-course closure without a success.

The candidate hypothesis is now specific: retain the parent’s rate-closed anterior gait—the only mechanism that escaped the curl—and make measured body-frame course error bias its desired mean yaw, instead of driving a half-cycle directly. This tests whether route demand can shift the parent’s phase-correlated stabilizing loop without losing the coherent carrier; it is a feedback-structure change, not gain-only tuning. I’m recording that diagnosis before touching the policy, as required.

The policy and durable lesson are both updated. The lesson now explicitly records that direct bearing and direct course selectors failed despite coherent wakes, and narrows the next reusable test to route bias inside the parent’s rate-closed carrier. I’m moving through the mandated static contract checks now; I will not run CFD.

The configured checker could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account. I’ve still invoked it as required; I’m running the exact three commands from its configuration manually so the candidate receives the same deterministic checks, without CFD.

The first deterministic check exposed a workspace metadata defect: `README.md` lists the same guidance parent twice, so the checker sees two assigned parents. I’m removing only that exact duplicate marker, then rerunning the check; this does not change the solver or experimental contract.

All three configured checks now pass manually: reusable-guidance semantics, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary. The offline replay of the parent trace also shows the new course term changes mean half-cycle authority from roughly `0.13` to `0.30` at the largest miss while keeping it well below the direct-selector saturation pattern; that is the intended bounded structural test, not a claimed CFD outcome.

Implemented exactly one candidate: a speed-gated body-frame course error biases the parent’s rate-closed anterior half-cycle controller while preserving its coherent traveling-bend carrier.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:60)

Validation passed:

- Guidance semantic-change check
- Julia policy/schema contract
- Solver boundary check

The configured checker agent’s pinned model was unavailable, so I ran its exact three commands manually. No CFD was run. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent entry from `README.md` that initially broke the guidance checker.
